rubric_notes: All must_include met: SCOPe 2.08 hierarchy with SUNIDs (a 46456, a.22 47112, a.22.1 47113) and all four curated families with correct SUNIDs and protein members; fold holds only one superfamily; superfamily is the homology-bearing level. a.22.1.0 'not a true family' annotation supported. Family distinctions preserved and transfer of nucleosome assembly, complex membership, DNA-binding mode, oligomeric state or template interchangeability explicitly denied, with external evidence named. Linker histones a.4.5.13 (46827) lineage matches bundle, sharing only class with core histones. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

Full correct hierarchy for both domains (class a, fold a.204, superfamily a.204.1 SUNID 101386, families a.204.1.2 and a.204.1.4), domain boundaries, species, and the fold-level homology_not_implied_above_superfamily warning, all supported by the bundle. Identifies the superfamily as the deepest shared homology-bearing node, rejects same-family placement, and refuses transfer of HisE substrate, reaction, pathway role, ligand preferences, oligomeric state and whole-protein function to the MazG-like structural-genomics target, listing needed external evidence. Complete. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-16.

All identifiers correct and bundle-supported. Remote homology and shared ATPase-domain core inferred from superfamily; explicit refusal to transfer whole-protein role, templates, substrate, reaction, ligand, regulation, oligomeric state or pathway. Correctly notes HSP70 peptide-binding domain is classified elsewhere (b.130.1) and cites the duplication comment. Complete.

Complete and bundle-supported: 2.08 hierarchy, superfamily 47240 with bimetal-centre comment, family SUNIDs, fold core annotation. Interprets as probable common ancestry at superfamily depth with chemistry diversifying after family splits; distinguishes this from mere fold sharing and from same-family assignment; rejects transfer of chemistry, metal, mechanism, regulation, oligomeric state; lists required structural, ligand, sequence, biochemical, and phylogenetic evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-16. Correct families with SUNIDs, superfamily b.6.1 (49503) as the homology-bearing level, fold b.6 (49502), protein node 110108 (verified). States remote probable common ancestry, not same-family. Cites family annotations lacking the metal-binding site versus superfamily copper-site comment and explains metal binding is not universal among descendants. Rejects copper/electron-transfer/template transfer and lists external evidence (conserved coordinating residues, metal-bound structures, biochemical assays, phylogenetic support). Complete.

All SCCS codes, SUNIDs, superfamily/fold/class placement correct and supported by evidence; remote homology at superfamily level stated. Rejects transferring Ras binding and generic ligand/pathway annotations, but never explicitly addresses ubiquitination/covalent conjugation or p97 binding as non-universal functions.

Correctly identifies c.23.1.1 (52173), c.23.1.4 (52252), c.23.1.5 (82344) as distinct families under CheY-like superfamily c.23.1 (52172) in fold c.23 (52171), release 2.08; all identifiers match the evidence bundle. States superfamily as the deepest homology-bearing node supporting probable common ancestry while keeping families distinct. Explicitly rejects transfer of receiver phosphorylation/phosphotransfer, KaiA circadian regulation, ODC whole-enzyme function and decarboxylase chemistry; treats the wing as a domain rather than the enzyme. KaiA 'lacks canonical receiver domains features' comment is supported by the 82344 annotations body. Names external evidence needed. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-16.

Full lineage with SUNIDs (310706, 310616, 310577, 51229), sibling superfamilies named, superfamily-scoped homology claim, V1 and A1 nodes sharing family b.84.5.1, fold membership = structural similarity not homology assertion, explicit caveat that separation does not prove convergence or nonhomology, rejects function/template transfer, notes PubMed 19893485 and absence of curator rationale in API. Release 2.08 stable supported by /releases/current in bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-16.

Complete. Correct SCCS/SUNIDs and class, children endpoint and homology warning accurately used, superfamily comments (f.21.1 ligand conservation, f.21.2 one- vs two-chain fold, f.21.3 possible link) correctly paraphrased and supported by bundle. States clearly this is negative-at-superfamily, not proof of analogy/convergence; lists sequence, structural alignment, heme-ligand/motif, domain-context, phylogenetic, literature evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

All three families (c.2.1.1/51736, c.2.1.8/51900, c.2.1.9/63944), superfamily c.2.1/51735, fold c.2 and class c correctly stated and supported by the bundle (children, parents, homology endpoints). Correctly places homology at the superfamily level, notes fold-level does not imply homology, rejects transfer of substrate, reaction, CoA specificity, channel role, cofactor, regulation, oligomeric state and whole-protein function, and names required external evidence. Correctly reports the c.2.1.1 family comment and PF02254 mapping as supported by annotations.

Complete: full lineage class k / k.40 / k.40.1 / k.40.1.1 with family SUNID 100905 and 'not a true family' comment; explicitly explains that the shared family would normally imply the closest relationship but the annotation overrides it, yielding a caveated designed-protein grouping. Notes separate protein/species nodes, rejects transfer of sequence, lineage, ligand binding, oligomeric state, template status, and names external evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

Complete and accurate: 1.69 d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 (own fold c.137) vs d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 residues 1-118 in c.23.14.2 under shared superfamily c.23.14 with 1f8y in c.23.14.1; l.1.1.1 tag artifacts d1t1ja2/d1t1jb2 correctly excluded from the comparison. Interprets the change as a new probable-common-ancestry hypothesis at superfamily level, cites the family comment on predicted deoxyribosyltransferase activity (supported by bundle) without over-transferring function, and states what external evidence would be needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

All must_include met: d1a14h2 H:1-8 synthetic N-terminal tag, class l Artifacts, l.1.1.1, SUNID 343393; d1a14h1 H:9-111 biological V-set b.1.1.1 under b.1.1; tag similarity not homology evidence, with the SCOPe artifact warning cited and supported by the bundle. Rejects homology, function, and template transfer through the tag, recommends excluding/stratifying tag matches, and states that construct context needs external evidence. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-16.

Complete: 1.75 single domain, 2.01-2.03 retained, 2.04 split through 2.08, correct boundaries/SUNIDs/classifications; uses supported 1.75 fold comment. Notes shared-root/no-positive-homology, boundary-aware searches, rejects function/calcium-state/template transfer, states limits.

Correct five-domain inventory with SIDs, boundaries, SCCS, and fold/superfamily/family names; d3jb9a5 A:47-697 correctly identified as the Prp8-specific new fold d.394 with single-child lineage supported by the bundle. Bromodomain family co-members (CBP, GCN5, P300/CAF, TAFII250) are supported by the children endpoint. Distinguishes shared-family relationship from Prp8-specific families nested in broader superfamilies, states mosaic/reuse interpretation, declines function transfer, and reports that annotation caveat records were empty.

Places all three in family a.298.1.1 with correct SUNIDs (267609/267596/267589), explains length varies with repeat count, and correctly reads the re heterogeneity flag on d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_ plus the d4cj9a_ representative repeat 4cj9 A:259-292. Rejects DNA-target/RVD/template transfer. All claims match its bundle.

Correctly reports stable 2.08 / 2.08-stable with freeze and release dates and the bundle-supported periodic label 2.08-2026-08-16 (accepted as a bundle-supported live value in place of the frozen 2023-01-06 label). Recommends citing 2.08 and preserving the full dated label when using periodic records; avoids both must_avoid items. Omits what the periodic label means in content terms (newly classified PDB entries added without rewriting older stable-release domains); only hedges that metadata alone cannot show what changed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

Complete and supported: SIDs/SUNIDs for all domains, shared a.47.2.1 lineage, three-helical fragment/spectrin comment and ms record, d1dn1b_ automated match to d3c98b_ within the Syntaxin 1A N-terminal branch, STAT-like fold described as four-long-helix bundle with homology-not-implied-above-superfamily warning. Correctly reframes fragments as partial observations of the family core, warns against treating the missing helix as a deletion or fragments as benchmark representatives, and lists external evidence needed for stronger claims. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

Cites c.1/c.1.7/c.1.7.1, c.2/c.2.1, c.25/c.25.1 with class c as deepest shared node, all supported by parents endpoints; the c.25.1 comment 'binds NADP differently than classical Rossmann-fold' is in its annotations evidence. Divergence within superfamily/family vs convergence across folds stated with the explicit caveat that hierarchy does not prove independent origin; evidence integration and transfer limits complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-16.

All stated classifications, SUNIDs, and boundaries correct; shared superfamily b.18.1 vs distinct families well argued, with honest statement that the API did not expose alignment, core residues, or the curator paper. Gives topology and functional context but omits the literature/sequence homology evidence type the question requests, so capped at 3.

Complete: SCOPe 2.08 lineage with correct SUNIDs (46690 family, 125655 domain) all supported by bundle; hf correctly defined as domain-scoped heterogeneous fold (different fold than exemplar, similar sequence and SSE count) that qualifies structure without deleting family homology. Rejects drop-in template use, routine same-family positive examples, and transfer of helix packing/DNA contacts/mutation effects; requires preserving or stratifying the hf label and external alignment/biochemical evidence. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

Complete and well supported. Correct hierarchy with SUNIDs, boundaries, protein nodes, release 2.08, fr inconsistency and heterogeneity records, d1o5dt1 sibling domain, CR9 complex. Family/superfamily homology vs fold/class architecture. Align only over present core with absent region masked; fragment usable only as labeled partial example, excluded/stratified for complete-domain benchmarks; quality values (0.28747195 X-ray 2.05 Å vs 0.02158265 NMR, effective resolution 4.0) correctly reported and correctly limited to technical ranking among comparable coverage; truncation not counted as distinct architecture; function-transfer caveats. All values match bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-16.

Correctly recommends new superfamily in existing fold, explains family as stronger homology claim, says new fold is wrong if the known fold match is real, and lists external evidence needed for stronger placement. Hierarchy order and homology-bearing levels match the /api/v1/levels bundle. Omits that a separate superfamily does not assert nonhomology/convergence and does not explicitly frame the placement as a revisable evolutionary hypothesis; the requirement that a new fold needs a distinct topology is only implicit. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-16.

All identifiers verified: class d, fold d.144, superfamily d.144.1, families d.144.1.4 (56171), d.144.1.6 (64411), d.144.1.7 (88854), release 2.08. Correctly states homology only at the superfamily level, interprets the fold-level 'homology_not_implied_above_superfamily' warning appropriately, and caveats the ATP-grasp/PIPK comment. Names every unsafe transfer (protein-kinase substrate/activation-loop, APH aminoglycoside binding, PI3K lipid/membrane/regulatory-subunit control) and lists sequence alignment, structural superposition with ligand/transition-state analogs, biochemical assays, and domain-context evidence. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-16.
